clue.text: Airline stops virus I found on operating system — one that acted monstrously

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so the airline sits inside the virus like a cork

parts.note: a bug is an informal word for a virus or infection
El Al is the Israeli national airline
taken as written
OS is the standard abbreviation for operating system

explanation.surface: A flight is grounded by a computer virus found on its operating system.
explanation.walkthrough: Bela Lugosi was the Hungarian-American actor famous for playing Dracula; the airline is the Israeli one, not BA.
explanation.definitionFit: Bela Lugosi was the horror-film star who played Count Dracula, so he acted the part of a monster.

clue.text: Knock bishop down

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
feeling down is feeling low

explanation.surface: A chess move or a brawl in which a bishop is knocked to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A knock and a blow are both synonyms for a hit or a setback.

clue.text: Oddly missing clues Geoff left group of doctors after rolling joint?

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters go missing, leaving only the even-placed ones behind

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of the two words
L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: something rolling turns over, so the doctors' group is read backwards

parts.note: the BMA is the British Medical Association, the doctors' professional body

explanation.surface: Geoff, short of clues, leaves a gathering of doctors after rolling a joint of cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's rolled joint is a cannabis cigarette; the definition is the butcher's kind of joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg of lamb is a classic cut of meat for roasting, which is what a butcher calls a joint.

clue.text: Band with new material

parts.note: a band or stripe can be a line
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A music group signs up with some fresh material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' and 'material' suggest a group and its songs, but the band is a stripe and the material is cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a fabric woven from flax, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Something to make you feel full of fuel — shake making energy expand

definitions.text: Something to make you feel full

indicators.note: the energy letter is swapped for a word meaning to swell up, so one letter is replaced by a longer piece

parts.note: gas is a fuel, and American petrol
in two shakes means in a trice, a moment
E is the physics symbol for energy
to balloon is to swell or expand

explanation.surface: A fuel-laden milkshake that bloats you with energy so you feel full.
explanation.walkthrough: The E of TRICE is replaced by BALLOON. A gastric balloon is an inflatable device placed in the stomach to help weight loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastric balloon fills part of the stomach so the patient feels sated after eating less.

clue.text: Appropriate heft and girth to be converted into warplane

parts.note: to appropriate is to take without permission

indicators.note: converted things are changed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both words, 'and' included only as a joiner

explanation.surface: Someone commandeers bulk and girth, intending to turn them into a military aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A stealth fighter is a combat jet designed to evade radar, a type of military aircraft.

clue.text: Drive taxi dropping Charlie to arrive at flat

parts.note: Dr is the street-name abbreviation for Drive

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it fall away, so one letter is left out

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Directions for a cab ride that drops someone called Charlie off at a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a home, but here it is an adjective meaning dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat and drab both describe something dull, lifeless and lacking colour.

clue.text: Strictly's third dancer wanting Jack Dee for example

indicators.note: third points to one letter, the one in position three of the word

parts.note: the third letter of Strictly

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter goes missing from the dancer

parts.note: someone who dances the jive
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A Strictly Come Dancing contestant lacking the comedian Jack Dee's style.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is the BBC ballroom show and Jack Dee is a deadpan British comedian, but the Dee here is a river in Wales, England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dee is one of several British rivers of that name, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Delivery over fourteen pounds for one of twelve gems

parts.note: a delivery in a maternity ward is a birth
a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A baby born weighing over fourteen pounds, set against a list of twelve gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' only places the weight after the delivery; it is not part of either piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Each calendar month is assigned a gem, so there are twelve birthstones in all.

clue.text: Vehicle partially ran aground when reversing

indicators.note: reversing goes backwards, so the concealed letters read right to left
only part of the phrase is used, so the answer sits inside it

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A car partly ran aground while being backed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle' suggests a car, but it means a medium of communication, as a party newspaper is its organ.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a means of expressing views, such as a journal, which is a vehicle for opinions.

clue.text: Stay the night right after police officer originally breaks cover

indicators.note: after places the first piece behind the rest of the build
breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: a record sleeve is a cover

indicators.note: originally points to the starting letters of the two words before it

parts.note: the first letters of each word
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A police officer breaks cover to arrest someone after a night of surveillance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' and 'breaks cover' suggest a stakeout, but cover is a noun for a record's outer wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepover is a night spent at someone else's house, so as a noun phrase it is a stay for the night.

clue.text: Clean up post office — everyone can see this is ultimately foolishly grand

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to mop is to clean a floor
PO is the abbreviation for post office
U is the film certificate for universal viewing

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so just the last letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of foolishly

explanation.surface: A complaint that an overblown post office clean-up in full public view is foolishly grand.
explanation.walkthrough: A U certificate means a film is suitable for all ages, so everyone can see it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompous means self-important and showily grand in manner, near-synonyms in the sense of pretentious.

clue.text: Student protest: amusing time to start sombre music?

indicators.note: to start tells the solver this pair of words comes first, ahead of the earlier ones

parts.note: fun used as an adjective, meaning entertaining
an era is a period of time
L is a learner, the plate on a student driver's car
a protest march

explanation.surface: A student protest that starts out as a fun outing, set to sombre music.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists Student and protest first, but amusing time is told to start, so FUN ERA leads.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral march is a slow, solemn piece played at burials, such as Chopin's, so it is mournful music.

clue.text: See 12
Ringo discovered McCartney half-cut inside covers?

indicators.note: dis-covered means with the covering removed, so the outside letters come off
half-cut means cut in half, so only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: Ringo Starr, the Beatles' drummer
Paul McCartney, his bandmate
taken as written before it is halved

explanation.surface: Ringo found Paul McCartney drunk ('half-cut') hiding under the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: Ringo's surname loses its outer letters and the word inside is cut to its first half. Half-cut is British slang for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpaulins are heavy waterproof sheets used to protect things, so they are covers.

clue.text: A 7 am start for actor initially inspires choice language

parts.note: taken as written
7-down's answer is RIVER, and R is its abbreviation
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of actor

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so each word gives its first letter

parts.note: the first letters of both words

explanation.surface: An actor's 7 am start inspires the choice of a language.
explanation.walkthrough: The 7 refers to the answer of 7-down, which is RIVER, abbreviated R.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic tongue, spoken in the Middle East in biblical times.

clue.text: Back garden or patio somewhat prepared for barbecue?

indicators.note: back means backwards, so the letters are read from the end
somewhat means to some extent, so only some of the letters are used

parts.note: the letters run across all three words

explanation.surface: A back garden or patio made ready for a barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a barbecue chef ties on an apron.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing an apron is dressed ready to cook, a playful way to describe getting set for grilling.

clue.text: Problem for cattle — maybe stop moving to and fro

parts.note: ho is an old call to stop, as in whoa

indicators.note: moving letters around shifts their order, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of to and fro, 'and' only joining them

explanation.surface: A farmer complains that cattle with a problem may stop moving to and fro.
explanation.walkthrough: Ho is a cry used to halt horses or attract attention, like whoa.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoof rot, or foot rot, is a bacterial infection of the feet of cattle and sheep.

clue.text: Hilarious person joining head of Scotland Yard's police division

parts.note: someone who is a riot is very funny

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Scotland
a quad, or quadrangle, is a courtyard

explanation.surface: A comedian joins the head of Scotland Yard's police unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters, is split: Scotland gives its first letter and Yard becomes a quad.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot squad is a police unit trained to control disorder, a section of the force.

clue.text: Turned up with books about Greek university's local courses?

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the next word is written back to front

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the books go around what follows

parts.note: B is book, doubled for the plural
Gr is the abbreviation for Greek
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A student turns up with books about a Greek university's local courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' suggests university studies, but they are courses of a meal; a local is a British word for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Pub grub is plain food served in a pub, so it is the meal courses at your local.

clue.text: See 4
Iron shirt on vacation and finally go on deck

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, so only the outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of shirt

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so just the last letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of go
taken as written

explanation.surface: Packing for a cruise: iron a shirt for the holiday, then head up on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like a ship's deck, but it is a verb meaning to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To festoon is to drape with garlands or decorations, as to deck the halls is to adorn them.

clue.text: See 5
Angler bends truth — essentially circulating far-fetched tales?

indicators.note: circulating letters move round and round, ending up in a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its very centre, so the middle letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of truth

explanation.surface: An angler stretches the truth, spreading tall tales about the one that got away.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: circulating also hints at how such stories spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban legends are implausible stories passed around as true, often about a friend of a friend.

clue.text: Boats at sea regularly keep moist

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Boats out at sea are routinely kept damp.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste is to spoon fat or juices over roasting meat so it stays moist.

clue.text: See 22
Charming, accommodating hotel's specialist area

indicators.note: accommodating means providing room for, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: nice means pleasant or charming
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A charming, welcoming hotel has carved out its own specialist area.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a specialised segment of a market or field, a narrow area of expertise.

clue.text: Visit son, 7

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
7-down's answer is RIVER, and the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.walkthrough: The 7 points to 7-down's answer, RIVER, for which the Tay is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A visit and a stay are both a period spent somewhere as a guest, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Thoroughly determined home team kicks off

indicators.note: kicking off means going first, so these words lead the build

parts.note: being in means being at home
a side is a sports team
out to do something means determined to do it

explanation.surface: A thoroughly determined home team kicks off the match.
explanation.walkthrough: The home team kicks off, so IN SIDE goes ahead of OUT even though 'determined' comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something inside out is to know it completely, so the phrase is an adverb for full knowledge.

clue.text: Muffin politician leaves in cellar, say

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so the politician exits from the muffin

parts.note: a crumpet is a griddle cake like a muffin
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician leaves a muffin down in the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cellar' looks like a basement, but it is a salt cellar; the 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruet is a small table container for salt, pepper or oil, so a salt cellar is one.

clue.text: Moved to avoid one foot drop

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so those letters are left out

parts.note: shifted means moved
I is the Roman numeral one
ft is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: Someone shifted aside to dodge a foot dropping down.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to let fall or cast off, as a tree drops its leaves.

clue.text: Cold as I dry funnel out

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are put into another order

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: Feeling the chill as someone dries out a funnel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold manner is one lacking warmth, so it is the same as being hostile or distant.
